mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar FEDFUNDS-up periods (p-value < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coincides with stronger consumer demand (HOUST), both leading to a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as improved labor market conditions fuel corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 50,000 in the prior month AND HOUST > 1,200
failure_condition: IC < 0.05 over 5 consecutive 60-day windows with positive signal (p-value threshold).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound within two months predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals a turning point in supply-side constraints.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 105 for two consecutive months then rises in the third
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in 30% of similar INDPRO-rebound events (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity (INDPRO) remains above 108 for three consecutive months, it indicates persistent supply constraints and a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not consistently negative across 40 such events (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it suggests a tightening labor market and stronger demand.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 3.5% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher than average in 10 such episodes (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of increasing payroll growth (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL) predict a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as wage growth is seen as sustainable and demand-driven.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases each month for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL growth < 0.2% over the same period

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, it predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not negative in >80% of such episodes (p < 0.01).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of over 1% for two consecutive months suggests deflationary pressure, leading to a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate lower inflation and potential rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls by >1% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly positive in 40 such CPIAUCSL declines (p > 0.05).
